title: Fresh Frozen Mouse Brain Preparation for Single Nuclei Sequencing
author: Chuck Vanderburg
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcbrism6

steps.title: Anesthetize and perfuse mouse
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse with 3 % isoflurane, then perform cardiac perfusion using ice‑cold HEPES‑Sucrose cutting solution (store the solution at 4 °C).

steps.title: Bisect head at cervical vertebrae
steps.instruction: Remove the head by bisecting between cervical vertebrae C2 and C3 with large scissors.

steps.title: Expose dural sheath
steps.instruction: Peel forward the cranial and facial skin and fat pads, remove the splenius capitis muscle with forceps, and expose the dural sheath covering the fossa between the foramen magnum and the first cervical vertebra.

steps.title: Pierce sheath and cut vertebrae
steps.instruction: Using a small pointed scissor, pierce the dural sheath in a rostral‑caudal direction, then cut the 1–2 cervical vertebrae along the dorsal midline.

steps.title: Snip skull along midline
steps.instruction: Insert the same scissors carefully 1–2 mm into the foramen magnum, press the lower blade upward against the inner skull edge, and snip the skull along the midline up through the intra‑orbital area over the olfactory bulbs.

steps.title: Remove cerebellar bone
steps.instruction: With a small toothed forceps, grasp the midline edge of the bone covering the cerebellum and gently push the bone hemisphere away; repeat until bone from the foramen magnum to the orbit is removed on both sides, taking special care not to tear the cerebellar paraflocculus.

steps.title: Expose brain and cut vessels
steps.instruction: Pick away the thick bone around the cribriform plate and orbit to fully expose the olfactory bulbs, gently roll the brain caudally using a blunt instrument (e.g., a small weighing spatula), cut the optic nerves with small scissors leaving the chiasma intact, then cut the carotid artery, followed by the basilar artery and any small cranial nerves, trying to cut rather than tear them.

steps.title: Wash and blot brain
steps.instruction: Wash the extracted brain in cold PBS to remove hair, blood, and debris; blot excess PBS gently so the brain remains moist but not submerged in liquid.

steps.title: Freeze brain for storage
steps.instruction: Place the whole brain in a 5 ml tube that already contains 2 ml of pre‑frozen OCT at the bottom, then store the tube at –80 °C until use.
